Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testLongLineChunkingIndentIgnored` in the `BugCLI162Test` class of the Apache Commons CLI library is supposed to test the chunking behavior of long lines in the `HelpFormatter` class. The test sets up an `Options` object with an option having a long description and then calls the `printHelp` method of `HelpFormatter` to generate the help message. The expectation is that long descriptions will be split and indented properly in the generated help message.

The current bug report describes an issue where the `HelpFormatter` class goes into an infinite loop and causes a JVM crash with an `OutOfMemoryError` when there is not enough space to display a word on a single line. The provided test case for the bug report demonstrates this issue by setting the width of the formatter to 20 and printing help for an option with a long description.

To diagnose the root cause of the infinite loop and JVM crash, we need to inspect the implementation of the `printHelp` method in the `HelpFormatter` class to understand how it handles long lines and word wrapping.

I will start by examining the `HelpFormatter.printHelp` method in the Apache Commons CLI library to identify any potential issues with word wrapping and line chunking.

Let's proceed with investigating the code snippet for the `printHelp` method in the `HelpFormatter` class.

messages.content:
The `renderWrappedText` method in the `HelpFormatter` class is responsible for rendering and wrapping the text to fit within the specified width. The method identifies the wrapping positions for the text and ensures that each line is properly padded with spaces.

Upon inspecting the implementation of the `renderWrappedText` method, the issue causing the infinite loop and JVM crash in the `HelpFormatter` class seems to be related to the loop structure for wrapping text at each line. The while loop within the method iterates indefinitely, leading to an infinite loop scenario that eventually exhausts memory and causes the JVM to crash with an `OutOfMemoryError`.

To address this issue, the loop structure within the `renderWrappedText` method needs to be revised to ensure proper termination conditions for wrapping the text within the specified width without entering an infinite loop.

The method that needs to be fixed:
- `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(java.lang.StringBuffer,int,int,java.lang.String)`

Let's recommend this method for fixing.
Recommendation:
```
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(java.lang.StringBuffer, int, int, java.lang.String)
```
